sample_unit: patients (referral cohort: 747 referred, 99,849 not referred; diagnosis cohort 419)
unlisted_practices: Semi-automated feature selection incorporating public knowledge graph data for rare disease prediction models
Prospective outreach and biochemical testing of patients flagged by the model (only 10 of 372 recruited, all negative)
Post hoc estimation of time saved to diagnosis (71% of cases identified earlier, 1.2 years saved)

screen.reason: The study develops and retrospectively evaluates machine learning models to detect acute hepatic porphyria and attempted prospective patient outreach/recruitment for testing, but does not test a specific organizational safeguard or deployment practice.
